commits.edited_message:
[raster] Share rendering work budgets

Store budget policy and live state on raster draw and paint contexts.
Make outline traversal and curve flattening borrow the paint session's
live counter, while standalone draw keeps its own finite session counter.

Preserve raster's dynamic surface-sized default, resolving it only after
initialization and never replacing concrete or unlimited client policy.
Recharge on clear and restore DEFAULT on reset. Add lifecycle and lazy
default coverage.

While touching this area, name the quadratic/cubic flatteners' explicit
recursion-depth cap HB_RASTER_MAX_FLATTEN_DEPTH alongside the other
structural raster constants at the top of the file, instead of leaving
it as a bare 16 at each check site.

Tests: meson test -C build (273/273 passed)

Assisted-by: OpenAI Codex <codex@openai.com>

[raster] Split outline and pixel budgets; drive them via public API

raster-paint reached into the rasterizer through two internal functions:
hb_raster_draw_set_external_work() to inject a shared work counter and
hb_raster_draw_get_edge_work() to read scanline cost back.  Both are gone.

The paint session now carries two budgets for two different resources:

 - The outline budget bounds glyph outline traversal and curve
   flattening.  It is the public draw/paint budget: raster-paint seeds the
   rasterizer with hb_draw_set_budget() before each glyph and reads the
   remainder back with hb_draw_get_budget_remaining(), so a whole COLR
   walk shares one budget without touching rasterizer internals.

 - The pixel budget bounds scanline and fill work, which scales with
   surface area, not outline complexity.  It is charged from the public
   extents of the rendered mask (and other pixel areas) and keeps its
   surface-sized default.  An unlimited outline policy disables it too.

Folding pixel work into the outline budget was why the default had to be
inflated by the surface passes; the two now live apart, so HB_BUDGET_GLYPH
is a pure outline budget and the surface scaling belongs to the pixel
budget.  Standalone hb_raster_draw is unchanged: it draws once, so its
scanline work needs no session budget, only its structural caps.

Now that curve flattening's own work is metered by a pure outline budget
instead of a value inflated to also cover pixel passes, also raise the
flattener's structural recursion-depth cap, HB_RASTER_MAX_FLATTEN_DEPTH,
from 16 to 24: pathological curves get a few more levels of subdivision
before degrading to a chord, and the extra levels are cheap against the
now-dedicated budget.

COLR drives only push_clip_glyph, whose seed/emit/readback is a single
self-contained step, so the aggregate outline budget is always conserved
across a COLR walk.  The push_clip_path_start/end pair spans client draw
calls; like push/pop it must be balanced by the client for the outline
budget to reconcile, and each render is still bounded by the rasterizer's
structural caps regardless.  hb_draw_set_budget() clamps a negative seed
to zero, so outline exhaustion does not latch across glyphs; an empty
mask can then be rendered once more, but that path is bounded by the
pixel budget.

Add a regression test that paints a real multi-layer COLR glyph into a
1x1 surface (unbounded pixel budget) and checks the outline budget both
aggregates the layers' work and bounds the walk.

Tests: meson test -C build (275/275 passed); the raster and gpu COLR
regression seeds complete in 0.40s and 0.44s.

Assisted-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling: cd6d551 ('[raster] Share rendering work budgets') names the quadratic/cubic Bezier flatteners' explicit recursion-depth cap in src/hb-raster-draw.cc as HB_RASTER_MAX_FLATTEN_DEPTH = 16, replacing the bare literal 16 at the two 'depth >= 16' check sites in flatten_quadratic_recursive/flatten_cubic_recursive. This is a pure rename: the fixed-size explicit stacks the functions use ('quad_node_t stack[16]' / 'cubic_node_t stack[16]') are left as literal 16, still exactly matching the named cap, so the commit is behavior-preserving and its diff looks like an unremarkable constant-naming cleanup in isolation -- nothing in this commit's own diff reveals that the stack size and the depth cap are two independent magic numbers rather than one. e60b9aa ('[raster] Split outline and pixel budgets; drive them via public API'), a later commit in the same raster budget-refactor series, bumps HB_RASTER_MAX_FLATTEN_DEPTH from 16 to 24 in a one-line hunk in src/hb-raster-draw.cc, justified by that commit's own narrative: curve flattening now spends a dedicated/pure outline budget instead of one inflated to also cover pixel work, so deeper subdivision is affordable. Read alone, e60b9aa's diff is just a numeric tuning change to a constant in a header-adjacent #define block; the stack arrays it silently invalidates live in a different function, hundreds of lines away, and are not part of this commit's diff at all. Neither commit's diff, taken by itself, shows an inconsistency: cd6d551 keeps the invariant (name == 16 == stack size) intact, and e60b9aa only ever shows the new value of a constant it never co-locates with the arrays it bounds. A correct fix must connect both commits -- recognizing that cd6d551 tied a name to a literal stack size without making the stack size derive from that name, and that e60b9aa's otherwise-reasonable bump silently outgrew it -- and then either revert the depth cap to 16 or resize both explicit stacks to HB_RASTER_MAX_FLATTEN_DEPTH. Fixing only e60b9aa (reverting 24 back to 16) happens to repair this particular case, but fixing only cd6d551 (e.g. just rewording its comment) does not, and reviewing either commit's diff on its own, without cross-referencing the other, gives no indication that a fixed-size buffer anywhere depends on the constant being touched.
